analysisSummary: PIN/QUOTE CHECK: git rev-parse HEAD = 9007ba1352e606575e32456512e25c41a9bf449c, tree clean, re-verified before writing. Hunter quotes are substantively accurate but line numbers drift by a few lines (investigated, immaterial): initializeAccount is contracts/Nexus.sol:306-334 (Hunter: 305-333); _initializeAccount is 336-356 (Hunter: 336-353); execute is 144-157 (Hunter cited 153-157); executeFromExecutor is 162-185 (Hunter: 166-180); PREP !isInitialized() require is line 129 (Hunter: 126); _installValidator is 216-235 with withHook/withRegistry at 222-223 (Hunter: 218-227); K1 onInstall require is K1Validator.sol:79 (Hunter: 79-82, correct). Commit 0b64d29 ('fix relay reinit') verified via git show: it added ONLY the !isInitialized() require inside the relay branch (now Nexus.sol:320-322). MECHANISM CONFIRMED AS CODE FACT: initializeAccount (Nexus.sol:306-334) wraps ALL guards in `if (msg.sender != address(this))`, so the self-call branch skips the transient-flag check (Initializable.requireInitializable, else-branch line 330), the relay signature + !isInitialized() + replay checks (lines 314-328), and any !isInitialized() check, then unconditionally runs _initializeAccount (line 333). _initializeAccount (336-356) parses a caller-supplied bootstrap address + bootstrapCall from initData head via assembly (342-348) and runs `bootstrap.delegatecall(bootstrapCall)` (350) with no allowlist; the post-check `require(isInitialized())` (353-355) passes trivially on an already-initialized non-7702 account and is skipped entirely for 7702 accounts. The self branch is BY DESIGN for 7702 first-init: natspec at Nexus.sol:304-305 says 'When a 7702 account is created, the first userOp should contain self-call to initialize the account.' The missing guard is therefore a real defense-in-depth gap, but the SECURITY CLAIM (High, limited-principal takeover bypassing hook/registry) FAILS on reachability and incremental impact, traced below. REACHABILITY (a) EntryPoint userOp -> execute() self-call: execute() (Nexus.sol:144) is onlyEntryPoint + withHook; _handleSingleExecution (ExecutionHelper.sol:205-213) decodes an arbitrary target with NO denylist (grep confirms none) and _execute (ExecutionHelper.sol:39-56) uses a raw CALL, so target==address(this) arrives at initializeAccount with msg.sender==address(this). BUT the outer userOp must first pass validateUserOp (Nexus.sol:102-138): nonce-mode dispatch (NonceLib) gives validate mode (no special handling), enable mode (_enableMode installs one module, then validates), or PREP mode (line 129 requires !isInitialized() BEFORE _initializeAccount at line 132, so PREP cannot re-init). _handleValidator (ModuleManager.sol:637-644) resolves address(0) to the default validator and otherwise REQUIRES the validator be installed. The ONLY validator shipping in-repo is K1Validator (verified: contracts/modules/ contains only K1Validator.sol; no session/policy validator, executor, or hook ships in-repo; SCOPE.md confirms session modules live outside this repo and out of bounty scope). K1Validator.validateUserOp (K1Validator.sol:147-149) checks ONLY an owner ECDSA signature over userOpHash via _validateSignatureForOwner(getOwner(...)) with NO callData/policy inspection; getOwner (191-194) falls back to the account itself when uninitialized. So with the default/in-repo validator, the 'attack' requires the OWNER'S OWN KEY: the owner re-initializing their own account is self-action, not attacker use (Q1 fails). (b) executeFromExecutor(): onlyExecutorModule (ModuleManager.sol:66-69, sender must be in the executors sentinel list) + withHook + withRegistry (Nexus.sol:162-170). Executor installation is itself owner-gated: installModule is onlyEntryPointOrSelf (Nexus.sol:226) reached only via a validated userOp or self-call, through _installExecutor with withHook+withRegistry (ModuleManager.sol:250-262). An installed executor is a fully-trusted principal that ALREADY gets arbitrary CALLTYPE_DELEGATECALL via executeFromExecutor (see Impact) — no new principal, no privilege gain. (c) Direct 7702 EOA self-transaction: VERIFIED semantics — for a 7702-delegated EOA (detection: ModuleManager.sol:624-635, extcodesize 23 + 0xef0100 prefix), a top-level transaction FROM the EOA TO itself executes Nexus code with msg.sender == tx sender == EOA == address(this), so a direct initializeAccount call skips the guards. But ONLY the holder of the EOA private key can originate a transaction with msg.sender == the EOA (ECDSA tx authentication; no other party can spoof msg.sender). Any other caller (EntryPoint, relayer, third-party contract) has msg.sender != address(this) and hits the guarded relay branch (owner signature + !isInitialized(), Nexus.sol:314-328). So this path is owner-only self-action, and it is the SAME key the relay branch trusts. (d) Nested calls: NO new path. Hook preCheck/postCheck (withHook, ModuleManager.sol:73-84), fallback handlers (_fallback CALLs handler, ModuleManager.sol:660-700 approx), and validators are all CALLED BY the account, so if they call back into the account msg.sender is the MODULE address, not address(this), and the guarded branch applies. The only other account-originated self-CALL in the codebase is _enableMode's `this.installModule(...)` (ModuleManager.sol:174) with a FIXED selector (installModule, not initializeAccount). executeUserOp (Nexus.sol:190-196) uses address(this).delegatecall, which PRESERVES msg.sender==EntryPoint, so initializeAccount reached that way hits the GUARDED branch — a counterexample to 'any execute path reaches the self branch'. executeComposable (Nexus.sol:201-203, onlyEntryPoint+withHook -> _executeAction -> _executeMemory CALL) can self-call but admits the same EntryPoint-validated principal as execute(). (e) Factory paths: NexusProxy constructor (NexusProxy.sol) calls setInitializable() then upgradeToAndCall(implementation, initializeAccount(initData)) via DELEGATECALL, so msg.sender is the factory/caller, NOT address(this): the classic transient-flag branch applies and requireInitializable() (Initializable.sol:30-39) CONSUMES the flag (tstore 0), single-use per deploying transaction (PR #302 fix). No factory path reaches the self branch. IMPACT — ZERO INCREMENTAL POWER FOR EVERY REACHABLE PRINCIPAL: the same principal (validated-userOp signer / installed executor), through the SAME outer validation and SAME outer withHook, can already do everything re-init offers and more: (1) execute()/executeFromExecutor() CALLTYPE_DELEGATECALL (Nexus.sol:144-157 and 162-185; ExecutionHelper.sol:227-237 _handleDelegateCallExecution -> 151-168 _executeDelegatecall, no target restriction, no denylist) runs ARBITRARY attacker-chosen code in account storage context with no _install* checks, no module-type check, no registry check — the IDENTICAL primitive to the bootstrap delegatecall, strictly a superset (any bootstrapCall is expressible as a delegatecall payload). (2) For proxy accounts, execute(CALLTYPE_SINGLE, self, upgradeToAndCall(attackerImpl,...)) replaces the implementation entirely (Nexus.sol:462 upgradeToAndCall; _authorizeUpgrade Nexus.sol:511-516 onlyEntryPointOrSelf, satisfied by self-call; blocked only for 7702). (3) execute(CALLTYPE_SINGLE, self, installModule(...)) installs an arbitrary module via _installModule (ModuleManager.sol:191-214) subject only to withHook/withRegistry/isModuleType checks — and withRegistry NO-OPS when no registry is configured (RegistryAdapter.sol:46-51, _checkRegistry returns silently if registry==address(0); registry is opt-in). (4) Direct fund drain via ordinary execute() calls. The Hunter's 'bypassing hook and registry checks' sub-claim is OVERSTATED: the outer execute()/executeFromExecutor() calls DO carry withHook (Nexus.sol:144,169), so the transaction IS hook-checked at the outer level (hook sees msg.sender=EntryPoint/executor and msg.data=execute(...)); the stock NexusBootstrap path ALSO runs withHook+withRegistry, because its _init* functions call _configureRegistry FIRST and then _installValidator/_installExecutor/_installHook/_installFallbackHandler/_installPreValidationHook (NexusBootstrap.sol:159-191, 247-248, 322-353, 413-423), each carrying withHook+withRegistry (ModuleManager.sol:222-223, 256-257, 282-283, 320-321, 375-376). Only a CUSTOM bootstrap that avoids _install* skips the inner checks — exactly as delegatecall-mode execute does. The hook-visibility difference (hook sees `execute` selector, not `initializeAccount`) applies EQUALLY to installModule/upgradeToAndCall wrapped in execute(), so it is not incremental to initializeAccount. The finding therefore requires a hypothetical validator policy that permits a self-targeted initializeAccount call while FORBIDDING the strictly-equivalent delegatecall-mode execute, installModule self-call, and upgradeToAndCall self-call. No such validator exists in-repo, no evidence supports such a policy shape (no sane session policy whitelists the initializeAccount selector), and session modules are out of bounty scope. DEFENSES CHECKED (honest accounting — defenses do NOT block the mechanism; the verdict rests on principal/impact, not on them): K1Validator.onInstall (K1Validator.sol:77-79) reverts ModuleAlreadyInitialized if already initialized for the account, so a NAIVE stock-bootstrap replay via initNexusWithDefaultValidator* (NexusBootstrap.sol:66-72, 161) reverts at the default-validator onInstall and the whole re-init rolls back (require(success), Nexus.sol:352) — but this blocks only the stock default-validator replay, not a custom bootstrap or a stock call installing only fresh modules; _installHook's HookAlreadyInstalled require (ModuleManager.sol:287) and _installValidator's DefaultValidatorAlreadyInstalled revert (227) similarly constrain only the _install* path. NexusBootstrap has NO onlySelf/onlyProxy guard and NO initialization flag (verified: all initNexus* functions are bare external payable, NexusBootstrap.sol:66-423) — no defense there. PREP (Nexus.sol:129) and relay (322) !isInitialized() guards and the transient-flag consume (Initializable.sol:30-39) all EXECUTE on their own paths but none applies to the self branch — confirmed. SentinelList push/init duplicate semantics could not be verified locally (node_modules/sentinellist absent from the checkout) and are NOT relied on for this verdict. DEDUP: NOT a root-cause duplicate of EX-116 (GHSA stale transient flag: classic-path SECOND call in the deploying transaction passing requireInitializable because the flag was never cleared — different guard, different trigger; H-B1's self branch never consults the flag at all, so it IS a distinct mechanism from EX-116 and the EX-116 Hunter warning does not kill it), NOT EX-049 (Zenith L-1: default validator allowed to VALIDATE without isInitialized() — validation gating, not re-init), NOT EX-I20 (Cantina 5.5.20: initializeAccount never verifying a validator was installed — the post-check whose fix H-B1 notes passes trivially when already initialized; adjacent observation, different root cause: missing installed-validator check vs missing !isInitialized() guard on the self branch). PARTIAL OVERLAP ONLY: EX-067 (Pashov L-12, hook bypass via NexusBootstrap installs) shares the 'init-path installs skip hook checks' EFFECT for the stock-bootstrap element, and EX-073/EX-074 (session-key oracle-confusion escape) share the 'limited principal escapes scope' EFFECT — but both have different mechanisms (bootstrap lacking withHook; enable-mode/emergency-uninstall signature-oracle confusion), so neither is a root-cause duplicate of the self-branch guard skip. Dedup does not decide this finding; reachability/impact does. HUNTER CAVEATS ASSESSED: the Hunter's own concession is correct and fatal — 'a pure owner-key account gains nothing beyond the owner's existing power' — and the 'limited-scope validator/executor' precondition has NO in-repo instance: the only validator is all-or-nothing K1, the only executors are owner-installed fully-trusted modules, and the only other self-call principal is the 7702 EOA key holder. Q1 (attacker use distinct from the owner?) = NO in-repo; Q4 (incremental gain over what the same principal can already do?) = NO (delegatecall-mode execute + upgradeToAndCall are strictly equivalent-or-greater). The missing !isInitialized() check on the self branch is a genuine hardening suggestion (it would not break the intended 7702 first-init flow, where the account is uninitialized), but as a High-severity bounty finding it is DISPROVED: verified mechanism, no attacker use, zero incremental impact.
